text: RICHER / THAN YOU THINK! [phone screen prop: COMPARISON]
scene: A cartoon man with swept brown hair, round glasses, a smirking closed mouth and half-lowered eyelids stands at the left in a white T-shirt and blue jeans, one hand resting on top of a green piggy bank. The piggy bank carries a large white check mark on its side. A small phone lies on the floor at the bottom-left corner with a red screen reading COMPARISON, and a thick curved black arrow beneath the headline points back toward the piggy bank.
mechanism: A reassurance claim: the check-marked piggy bank plus the relaxed cartoon owner turns the title's 'better than you think' into a pass-mark on the viewer's own savings.
composition: The figure fills the left third at full height while a two-line headline takes the upper right; the piggy bank sits in the lower middle as the secondary focus. The arrow runs from the headline's end down-left to the pig, so the eye loops text, arrow, pig, face. White space around the headline keeps the frame uncluttered.
typography: Four words in two tiers: RICHER in very heavy black capitals at roughly twice the height of THAN YOU THINK! beneath it. Both tiers stay legible at 160x90, while the COMPARISON phone text is far too small to survive. The wording is a paraphrase of the title with nothing added.
colors: Almost entirely white, black and one saturated green. The green pig and its white check are the only strong colour and pull attention away from the muted skin, blue jeans and grey-white shirt; the small red phone screen is the only red.
psychology: The half-lidded eyes, flat smile and hand resting on the pig read as a relaxed pose. The check mark supplies a pass-mark cue, and nothing in the image suggests fear or urgency.
partnership: The title offers signs that you are doing better financially; the thumbnail restates that as RICHER THAN YOU THINK! and adds only a check mark. It does not say which signs, so the open question of what the signs are remains for the video.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the huge word RICHER first, then THAN YOU THINK!, then the black arrow to the green piggy bank, and last the man's face at the left.
art: Flat-colour cartoon with uniform black outlines and a clean cutout on white, in a family-sitcom drawing style with no visible compositing artefacts. The faint grey speckle in the white background is barely noticeable, and the pig and headline both remain clean at small size.
strength: The large green check-marked piggy bank answers 'am I okay?' with a single glance-sized symbol.
weakness: The headline is a restatement of the title, so the text supplies no new fact, and the COMPARISON phone prop is unreadable.
bottleneck: Nothing quantifies or names the signs, so the frame promises reassurance without any curiosity-gap detail.
action: Hypothesis: replace THAN YOU THINK! with a concrete figure on the pig (for example a dollar amount) to test whether a specific number beats the generic reassurance.
counterexample: Seq 4 uses the same sitcom-cartoon style but shows alarm and a falling chart, where this frame shows calm and a check mark.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: SO YOU WANT TO OWN / A HAIR SALOON / Startup Costs / Licenses & Permits / Equipment & Supplies / Location & Rent / Operating Expenses / Profit Margins / Marketing & Clients / Growth & Expansion [sign: HAIR SALOON] [chalkboard: RENT / SALARIES / UTILITIES / MARKETING / SUPPLIES / CUT / COLOR / STYLE / CARE / & MORE]
scene: A glossy salon interior sits in the centre: three round-bulb lit mirrors, three black barber chairs, a marble-and-gold reception counter with a monitor and potted plant at the left, product shelves at both sides, and a wooden A-frame chalkboard with a tool trolley at the right. A black sign above reads HAIR SALOON beside a gold profile head and scissors. Eight hand-drawn red ovals, four down each side, hold cost-category labels, each with a small black arrow aimed at the room.
mechanism: A labelled map of the business: the salon picture is annotated with eight cost and operations categories, so the image itself acts as a checklist of what ownership involves.
composition: A two-line headline spans the entire top, underlined by a red stroke, above a centred salon photo flanked symmetrically by four ovals per side. The layout is a tidy three-column grid with the room as the hub. Hierarchy is clear at the top but the eight satellite labels compete for second place.
typography: The 8-word headline is huge black capitals, with A HAIR SALOON on the second line in heavier, larger letters. The oval labels are thin handwritten text of two or three words each, and they dissolve into specks at 160x90. The words SO YOU WANT TO OWN restate the title's subject, while the oval labels add the cost categories the title only implies.
colors: White background with black headline, a warm black-and-gold salon interior and red hand-drawn ovals and underline as the accent. The gold lighting and bulb glow lift the salon off the white page.
psychology: No person is shown. The warm, aspirational salon interior reads as the dream of ownership, and the red-circled cost labels hint at the burden hidden behind it. The 'so you want to' framing addresses the viewer directly.
partnership: The title promises the economics of owning a salon, and the thumbnail supplies the scope as eight named cost areas. It mostly complements the title, though listing every category up front leaves less to discover.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the black HAIR SALOON headline first, then the lit mirrors at the room's centre, then the left-hand ovals from Startup Costs downward, and finally the right-hand column.
art: The interior is smooth and glossy with perfect symmetry, glowing bulbs and uniform reflections, paired with marker-style ovals and arrows pasted over it. The mix of render and doodles reads as a deliberate infographic collage. Background detail is dense with shelves, bottles and chairs, so the frame is visually busy.
strength: The headline and a recognisable, brightly lit salon establish the business topic immediately.
weakness: Eight thin handwritten labels plus a chalkboard of tiny items make the lower two thirds illegible at phone size.
bottleneck: With no face and no tension, the frame shows a pleasant room and a list but no point of conflict or stakes.
action: Hypothesis: cut the eight ovals down to one circled item, such as Profit Margins with a figure, to test whether a single focal question outperforms the full checklist.
counterexample: Seq 1 has a four-word headline and one prop, where this frame carries twenty-four words plus signage.
hero_object: lit-mirror salon interior with eight labelled ovals
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: [75+ badge] / AGES 75-85: / IF YOU STILL / DO THESE / 6 THINGS / YOU'RE IN TOP 1% [name tag: Dr. Sarah Mitchell, Internal Medicine]
scene: A dark-haired woman in green scrubs stands at the right with a closed-mouth smile and points her index finger toward the text. A white name tag on her scrub top reads Dr. Sarah Mitchell, Internal Medicine, which differs from the name in the title's credit line. A navy banner at the top carries two small gold elder silhouettes with canes and a gold circle reading 75+. The background is a gold grid.
mechanism: An authority-plus-flattery frame: a scrub-clad presenter points at a promise that doing six unnamed things puts a 75-85-year-old in the top 1 percent.
composition: The four-line headline fills the left 60 percent in a stack, with a navy plate holding the last line across the bottom, and the woman occupies the right 30 percent at three-quarter length. Her pointing hand reaches into the gap between text and figure, linking the two. The top banner adds a third horizontal tier.
typography: Fourteen words in white capitals on gold, with the last line in yellow on a navy plate. IF YOU STILL DO THESE 6 THINGS is the largest block, and the plate line YOU'RE IN TOP 1% is clearly secondary. All lines survive at 160x90, while the name tag text does not. The wording repeats the title's age range and six-things claim and adds the top 1% outcome.
colors: Mustard-gold ground, navy bars and plate, white and yellow type, and a deep teal-green scrub top. The gold-navy pairing gives strong contrast, and the green figure stands apart from the yellow ground without the palette signalling danger.
psychology: A gentle smile, direct gaze and an outstretched index finger read as a friendly instruction. The scrubs and name tag supply a medical-authority cue, while the top 1% wording offers pride rather than fear.
partnership: The title says if you still do these six things you are one of a kind; the thumbnail turns that into the top 1% claim and states the age range. It leaves open which six things, which preserves the curiosity gap.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the large AGES 75-85: line first, then the stacked white block IF YOU STILL DO THESE 6 THINGS, then the woman's face and pointing hand, and finally the navy YOU'RE IN TOP 1% plate.
art: Smooth, evenly lit portrait with a very clean cutout and no shadow on the grid, which gives a stock-image look. The name tag and its credential line are the only small details and they stay legible only at native size. The gold grid is simple and does not compete.
strength: A single flattering numeric claim (6 things, top 1%) with a pointing presenter makes the premise legible in one glance.
weakness: The name tag shows a different doctor name from the title's credit, which muddies who is speaking.
bottleneck: The six things are never hinted at, so the elderly viewer must trust an unnamed authority to reveal them.
action: Hypothesis: align the name tag with the channel name or remove it, to test whether a consistent credential strengthens trust.
counterexample: Seq 7 also targets seniors but uses a cartoon patient with no presenter or credential, where this frame leans on a scrub-clad figure.
medical_notes: The printed name tag (Dr. Sarah Mitchell) differs from the name in the title (Dr. Aliza Wright), so the speaker's credential is ambiguous from packaging alone.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A cartoon man with short orange hair, a large round chin, wide round eyes, and an open mouth wearing a grey T-shirt stands at the left. A grid chart in the centre carries a thick red zigzag line that falls from top-left and ends by piercing the roof of a small grey house with brown shingles. A red arrowhead sits at the house's window level at the lower right, with small pieces of rubble on the ground, and a curved black arrow runs from the ellipsis down toward the house.
mechanism: A collapse metaphor: a plunging red line literally stabs a house while a wide-eyed bystander reacts, turning a market-change title into a visible crash.
composition: The face occupies the left third and the headline the upper right, with the chart and house forming a lower-right diagonal from the peak at upper left down to the house at lower right. The black arrow connects the headline to the house. The staring eyes point right, in the direction of the chart.
typography: Two words in extra-heavy black capitals with a three-dot ellipsis, taking up the top right. Readable at 160x90 as a block. The text is a verdict not present in the title, which asks what happened, so it escalates the title.
colors: White ground, black headline and outlines, a pink face, a grey shirt, and a saturated red zigzag that is the only strong accent. The red line signals decline and alarm and is the brightest colour in the frame.
psychology: Round white eyes with small pupils and an open mouth read as shock. The falling red line and cracked rubble reinforce a loss cue, and the ellipsis adds a defeated tone.
partnership: The title shouts WTF about the housing market, and the thumbnail answers with a finality claim plus a crashing-house image. It escalates the tone, but a viewer may read the conclusion as already given.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the shocked face first, then IT'S OVER..., then the red zigzag line, and finally the house with the rubble.
art: Flat-colour sitcom-style cartoon with thick uniform outlines and clean cutouts on white. The chart is a simple hand-drawn-looking grid with no numbers, and all elements stay legible at small sizes.
strength: A single falling red line ending in a damaged house makes the housing-crash storyline readable without words.
weakness: The chart has no axis labels or numbers, so the decline is symbolic and carries no specific data.
bottleneck: IT'S OVER... states a conclusion without saying what is over, so the viewer cannot tell whether prices, rates or the market itself is meant.
action: Hypothesis: add a single price or percentage on the chart axis to test whether a concrete data point adds credibility to the collapse image.
counterexample: Seq 1 uses the same cartoon style with a calm smirk and a green check mark, showing the opposite emotional direction.
expression_label: wide round eyes with open mouth
hero_object: falling red line piercing a house
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: The frame is split down the middle. At the left is a desaturated grey scene of rickety stilt houses with broken planks and posts, and at the right a colour scene of three tall skyscrapers topped by a ship-shaped deck under a blue sky, with a stone lion-fish statue at the far right spouting an orange arc of water. A simple cartoon man with a black bob haircut, a furrowed brow, a flat mouth and a white shirt with a black tie stands in the middle, overlapping both halves.
mechanism: A transformation split: shabby stilt houses against a glittering skyline, with a stern presenter on the seam, make the title's one-generation build-up visible as a before and after.
composition: A strict two-half split with the figure centred on the seam at about 80 percent of frame height, and a label at the top centre of each half. The grey-to-colour contrast gives immediate polarity, and the orange water arc from the right adds a diagonal that sweeps toward the centre.
typography: Two words, 1950s and TODAY, in white capitals with dark outlines at the top of their halves. Both labels are readable at 160x90. The title carries the man and the country while the thumbnail adds the time contrast only.
colors: A monochrome grey half against a saturated blue, orange and violet half. The palette contrast carries the story, and the character's pale tan face stands out against both halves.
psychology: The slanted brows and flat mouth read as a stern look. The grey ruin versus bright skyline supplies a before-and-after hope cue, though the face itself shows no joy.
partnership: The title names the builder and the one-generation timeline, and the thumbnail illustrates the time contrast with two labels. The pair is complementary; the image never names the country in text, relying on the landmarks.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the central stern face first, then TODAY with the bright skyline, then the grey 1950s half, and finally the water arc at the right.
art: Flat-vector cartoon with thick outlines on the figure and softer gradients in the skyline and sky. The two halves differ in rendering weight, but the seam is clean and the figure overlaps it consistently. Detail in the planks and building windows is lost at small size, but the colour split survives.
strength: The grey-versus-colour split makes a one-generation transformation readable without reading any text.
weakness: The stern cartoon face suggests neither triumph nor struggle, so the emotional direction of the story is ambiguous.
bottleneck: The unnamed man is the only subject, and nothing in the frame says who he is or why he matters.
action: Hypothesis: add a numeric marker such as GDP or a year range on the skyline side to test whether specificity strengthens the transformation claim.
counterexample: Seq 8 also uses a two-panel split but contrasts two people and prices, where this frame contrasts two eras with one shared figure.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: YOUR FEET / WILL TELL / YOUR SUGAR / IS INCREASING [anatomical labels on image: Diabetic Neuropathy (Nerve Damage); Tendon Shortening; Peripheral Artery Disease (Poor Circulation); Skin Changes (Dryness, Cracking); Slow-healinglly Diabetic oot Foot Ulcer; Slow-healing Diabetic Foot Ulcer; Muscle Atrophy and Deformities]
scene: Two large photorealistic feet fill the right half against black: one seen from the side with prominent veins, and another showing the sole with a circular wound on the sole. A second round ulcer is visible on the side foot near the toes. Thin white leader lines run from small black-and-white labels to each area, naming conditions such as Diabetic Neuropathy and Peripheral Artery Disease. One label reads Slow-healinglly Diabetic oot Foot Ulcer, a visibly garbled string.
mechanism: A body-as-warning frame: a four-line claim that the feet reveal blood sugar rising is paired with annotated feet showing wounds, so the picture asserts a diagnostic link.
composition: A left column of four stacked text lines takes about 55 percent of the width, and the feet occupy the right 45 percent on a black field. The red bar under the last line anchors the bottom-left. Two parallel focal points exist, the headline and the sole, and the leader lines pull attention across the foot.
typography: Eight words in four lines of very heavy condensed capitals: YOUR FEET WILL TELL in yellow, YOUR SUGAR in white, and IS INCREASING in white on a red bar. The headline is readable at 160x90 as a block. The annotation labels are tiny and become unreadable at that size. The text makes a definitive claim that the title hedges with 'could mean'.
colors: Black background with yellow and white headline and a red bar, plus warm skin tones on the feet. The red bar and yellow are used as alarm signals, and the pale feet stand out sharply against black.
psychology: No face appears, so the emotional cue is bodily: visible wounds and the annotated disease names trigger a threat-to-health reading. The imperative tone reads as an alarm aimed at older viewers.
partnership: The title offers nine warning signs that could mean diabetes; the thumbnail states outright that the feet reveal rising sugar. It escalates the claim, and the ulcer imagery is a late-stage symptom, which makes the pairing risk overstating how common the signs are.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the large yellow YOUR FEET first, then the red IS INCREASING bar, then the sole with its wound at the right, and last the thin annotations.
art: Photorealistic foot renders with plausible skin texture and veins, overlaid with hand-set annotation text. The garbled label with its duplicated and missing letters is a concrete text artefact, and two near-identical labels repeat on the two feet. Clutter at the right reduces clarity at small sizes.
strength: The yellow-white-red headline and the big pale feet on black make the topic and the alarm tone clear within a glance.
weakness: A garbled annotation and ten micro-labels make the medical overlay look unreliable and illegible at phone size.
bottleneck: The definitive wording and wound imagery overstate what a title that says 'could mean' implies, so the claim and image stand ahead of the evidence the packaging gives.
action: Hypothesis: replace the annotated overlays with one labelled foot and the phrase CAN SIGNAL, to test whether a hedged claim keeps the alarm without the overstated diagnosis.
counterexample: Seq 3 uses a smiling presenter and a flattering claim, where this frame uses wounds and an alarm banner with no person.
medical_notes: The thumbnail states outright that the feet show rising sugar and pictures ulcers, while the title only says the signs could mean diabetes.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: DOCTOR REVEALS: / BEST SLEEP TIME / FOR YOUR HEALTH / AFTER 70
scene: A flat-vector elderly man with swept-back white hair, round glasses, closed eyes and an open mouth yawns with one hand raised to his chin. He sits up in bed wearing pink pyjamas with dark piping, a white pillow behind him and a green plaid blanket across his lap. An open book rests under his other hand, and the edge of a wooden bedside table shows at the lower right.
mechanism: A hidden-answer frame: a yawning older man in bed pictures the question of bedtime, while a headline promises that a doctor reveals the best time.
composition: Text occupies the left 60 percent as four stacked lines, with AFTER 70 in a red box at the bottom, and the bed scene fills the right 40 percent. The man's face sits near the upper right and the book at the lower middle; the blanket crops at the bottom edge.
typography: Ten words across four lines. DOCTOR REVEALS: and BEST SLEEP TIME are yellow capitals, FOR YOUR HEALTH is smaller and white, and AFTER 70 is large white on a red box. At 160x90 the yellow lines and AFTER 70 survive, while FOR YOUR HEALTH is the thinnest. The words echo the title's own phrase nearly verbatim.
colors: Pure black background, bright yellow and white type, and a red box as the accent. The pink pyjamas and teal-green blanket are the only cool-warm contrast in the picture, and the yellow-on-black pairing carries an urgent, alert tone.
psychology: A closed-eye yawn, a hand at the mouth and an open book read as tiredness at bedtime. The visible cues are drowsiness and routine, not distress, which fits an advice topic.
partnership: The thumbnail reuses the title's phrase doctor, best sleep time, health and after 70 and shows the sleeper, so it adds a visual rather than information. Neither the hour nor the doctor is named, which leaves the answer hidden.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow DOCTOR REVEALS: first, then BEST SLEEP TIME, then the red AFTER 70 box, and finally the yawning man.
art: Clean flat-vector illustration with smooth shapes and no outline weight variation, cut out on black. The man and bed are coherent and the book, pillow and blanket are clearly readable. The simple stock-style rendering has little texture, but it survives small sizes.
strength: The age marker AFTER 70 on a red box is the clearest cue to who the video targets.
weakness: The line FOR YOUR HEALTH is the smallest on the thumbnail and adds no information beyond the title.
bottleneck: The title asks what time to go to bed, but the image shows only a generic yawning sleeper, so nothing hints at an hour.
action: Hypothesis: print an actual clock time with a question mark on the bedside, to test whether a concrete number outperforms the abstract DOCTOR REVEALS opener.
counterexample: Seq 6 uses the same yellow-white-red-on-black scheme with an alarming wound image, where this frame uses a drowsy, low-threat picture.
expression_label: closed-eyed yawn with hand at chin
hero_object: yawning older man in bed with open book
medical_notes: The word Doctor appears without a named person or visible credential, so who is giving the sleep-time advice is unclear from packaging alone.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A two-panel comparison under a red headline. In the left panel, a cartoon man in glasses, a navy suit and a tie smiles and holds up a blue credit card showing 750 and a gold key. In the right panel, a similar man without glasses and with wide white eyes and an open mouth holds a red card showing 640 and a key, while a black arrow points from the card to his face and a burlap sack of dollar bills labelled $250,000 sits at his lower right.
mechanism: A paired contrast: a high score with a calm face against a low score with a screaming face and a $250,000 sack makes the title's credit-score claim a visible cost comparison.
composition: The frame splits into two equal bordered panels beneath a centred headline band, each holding a bust-length figure at about 55 percent of the panel height. The side-by-side pairing gives a quick good-versus-bad read, and the sack at the lower right anchors the final panel.
typography: Three headline words in red capitals with a black outline sit on a white band, and the card scores 750 and 640 plus $250,000 on the sack serve as numeric props. The headline reads clearly at 160x90, while the card numbers are blurry at that size. The title explains the claim, and the thumbnail adds the term the poor tax.
colors: White ground with a red headline, navy suits, a blue good card, a red bad card and green dollar bills. The red headline and red card are used as a danger cue against the calm blue card.
psychology: The left man shows a closed-mouth smile and relaxed brows, and the right man shows wide white eyes, angled brows and an open mouth. The contrast of calm against alarm sets up a reward-versus-penalty reading.
partnership: The title gives the $250,000 lie and credit-score-as-scam angle, and the thumbnail adds a new label, THE POOR TAX, together with a score pair that makes the money cost concrete. The pairing complements the title rather than duplicating it.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the red THE POOR TAX headline first, then the right-hand screaming face with the sack, then the red 640 card, and last the left smiling man with the 750 card.
art: Flat cartoon with consistent outlines and warm brown skin tones, with the two panels sharing identical suit and key props. Faces are expressive and the cutout against white is clean. The tiny digits on the cards and the card chips lose clarity at small sizes.
strength: The calm face against the screaming face with a $250,000 sack makes the cost of a lower score readable at once.
weakness: Card numbers 750 and 640 are small relative to the headline, so the score gap is hard to read at phone size.
bottleneck: The right-hand panel packs a card, key, arrow, face and sack into one corner, so the viewer must work out which element is the cause.
action: Hypothesis: enlarge the two score numbers to match the headline height to test whether making 750 versus 640 the visible hook improves the comparison read.
counterexample: Seq 5 also uses a two-panel split but contrasts two eras with one figure, where this frame contrasts two people and two numbers.
expression_label: smile on left, wide eyes with open mouth on right
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

mechanism: A lounging, cash-showered figure pictures early retirement as a finished state, while the headline pins the claim to a ten-year deadline.
composition: The reclining figure fills the left half with his head at upper left, and a two-line headline sits at the upper right. The black arrow runs from the lower end of the headline down-left toward his crossed legs, closing a triangle of text, arrow and man. The bottom right corner stays blank white.

The number line is the heaviest element, and everything stays crisp at 160x90. The words copy the title's retire-in-10-years phrase and omit its (So FEW) hook.
colors: A white field carries black type, a navy polo, a khaki bean bag, and one saturated accent, the neon-green glow around the floating bills. The orange-yellow box on RETIRE is the single warm highlight.
psychology: Wide round eyes, an open toothy smile, a hand behind the head and crossed legs read as an at-ease, celebratory pose. The money rain is a reward cue, and no threat cue is present.
partnership: The thumbnail echoes the title's retire-in-10-years claim and shows the payoff, but it drops the title's 'how much to invest' question and the (So FEW) twist. The image presents the destination with no hint of the monthly amount, which leaves the number unanswered.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the big 10 YEARS first, then RETIRE on its yellow box, then the black arrow down to the grinning man, and last the green banknotes around his head.
art: Smooth glossy cartoon with a consistent thick outline and a clean cutout on white, with a soft drop shadow under the bean bag. The green glow around the bills is a bit soft but remains coherent, and the figure's anatomy is consistent. Simple shapes keep the frame readable at small size.
strength: A man lounging in a bean bag under a rain of cash communicates early-retirement relief with no reading needed.
weakness: The text and image together convey only a goal, never the monthly figure the title asks about.

composition: The knight stands at centre-left, taller and nearer, with the rope above him running off the top edge; the king stands lower right on a diagonal, and his pointing arm directs the eye across to the knight. Two tag labels sit high, one over each figure. The diagonal stair and gallows lines lead toward the centre.

colors: Almost the entire environment is washed in white and pale grey, so the red cross, the crimson and gold robe and the yellow flag are the only saturated accents. The white world isolates both figures sharply.
psychology: The knight stands with a closed mouth and eyes turned left while bound, and the king shows lowered brows and a scowl while pointing. The noose and rope supply a threat cue, and the imbalance of power is visible.
partnership: The title says every king wanted this Templar dead and that he outlasted them all, and the thumbnail dramatises the first half with a noose and an accusing king. The outcome stays hidden, which gives the title room to supply the surprise.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the red cross on the knight's tunic first, then the yellow TEMPLAR flag, then the crowned king's pointing arm, and last the KING flag at the upper right.
art: A detailed 3D render with realistic faces, cloth wear and rope texture against a monochrome clay-style set. strength: The colour isolation of two figures in a white world, plus a noose, tells a clear victim-and-accuser story.
weakness: The faces are small within the frame, so the expressions that carry the tension are lost at phone size.
bottleneck: The noose reads as the answer to the title's 'wanted dead' premise, which does not signal the survival twist the title promises.
action: Hypothesis: crop closer on the Templar's face and the king's pointing hand, to test whether larger expressions lift the confrontation read at small size.
counterexample: Seq 11 also stages a single named character in a scene but with a label that states a wealth tier, where this frame uses two role labels.

scene: Under a heavy grey dusk sky, a pale cartoon man with tousled brown hair, round glasses, half-lowered eyelids and a flat mouth walks across a runway in a black suit and tie. Behind him are a white private jet with its door stair lowered, a black luxury sedan with an open door and a uniformed chauffeur, and a large yacht on the water at left. Open brown suitcases with banknote bundles sit at the lower right. A white label box at upper left has a curved black arrow aimed at his head.
mechanism: A wealth tableau: the jet, limousine, yacht and open cases of cash make the label's billion-dollar company visible as the lifestyle the title promises.
composition: The man walks near the centre, leaving the frame's right two thirds for the jet and cash cases and the left third for the car and yacht. The label and arrow run diagonally into his head from the top left. Each luxury item occupies its own zone, so the layout reads as a stage set rather than one focal point.
typography: Three words in a single line of bold black condensed capitals on a white box, $1B HOLDING COMPANY, at the upper left. The box is the only text, and at 160x90 it shrinks to a thin strip that is only just legible. It restates the title's final phrase and gives no verb or outcome.
colors: A dark, desaturated palette of storm-grey sky, black suit and black car, with a warm sunset band at the horizon and the white jet as the brightest mass. The only colour accents are the small green bundles in the cases and the brown leather of the suitcases.
psychology: The man's half-lidded eyes and level mouth give an unreactive look, and the walking posture with a waiting chauffeur reads as status. The moody sky adds a serious tone rather than celebration.
partnership: The title says you become wealthy by building a $1B holding company, and the thumbnail shows the payoff of that wealth without explaining how. It restates the label and adds the visual proof of status, so the how stays for the video.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the white jet first, then the walking man with the black arrow, then the white label box, and finally the open suitcases of cash at lower right.
art: The airport scene is a painterly, textured render with consistent dusk lighting, while the man is a simple cartoon with a smooth pale face, which gives a stylistic mismatch between figure and background. All objects are coherent. At small size the dark sky and car merge into one mass.
strength: Jet, limousine, yacht and cash cases together tell the billionaire story in a single glance.
weakness: The label box is the only text and shrinks to a thin strip at 160x90, so the $1B claim is hard to read at phone size.
bottleneck: The picture shows the result of wealth but nothing about holding companies, so the specific hook in the title does not appear visually.
action: Hypothesis: enlarge the $1B to roughly the height of the man's head to test whether the number alone, readable at small size, anchors the claim.
counterexample: Seq 9 uses a bright white field with one large headline, where this frame uses a dark crowded scene with one small label.
hero_object: private jet with cases of cash

scene: A vertical black line splits the frame under a one-line headline. At the left, a bearded man in round glasses, a blue suit and a tie smiles and holds a tablet showing a chart while gesturing toward a floating green panel with rising bars, a gold arrow and euro and dollar coins. At the right, a similar bearded man in a blue work shirt sweats with raised brows and a clenched grimace while writing on a stack of paper bills; a thought bubble shows a banknote bundle dropping into a hat beside a DEBT bubble.
mechanism: A fork-in-the-road comparison: a confident investor and an anxious payer face the same bearded model, so the question in the headline becomes two lives side by side.
composition: A headline band across the top is followed by two equal panels divided by a thin black line, each with a three-quarter-length figure. The left side is airy with pale-green chart ghosts, and the right side is dense with paper piles and a table. The figures mirror each other's size and position.
typography: Three words in extra-wide black capitals with a question mark, with DEBT? on a yellow highlight box. The headline spans the full width and is readable at 160x90. It reframes the title's payoff-versus-invest dilemma as a single provocative question.
colors: White ground with a clean black headline, a bright yellow highlight, a blue suit and shirt, and soft green for the investing panel. The green chart half reads cool and calm and the paper-covered right half reads cluttered and grey-white.
psychology: The left man shows raised brows, round open eyes and a closed smile, and the right man shows sweat drops, a clenched mouth and heavy lids. The expression gap sets up relief against stress.
partnership: The title frames debt payoff against investing as the decision keeping you up at night. The thumbnail turns it into IGNORE THE DEBT? and shows the two figures, so it escalates the stakes without naming either option explicitly.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the yellow DEBT? box first, then the sweating man on the right, then the confident man with the green chart on the left, and finally the thought bubble.
art: Clean cartoon linework with consistent character design across both panels and flat colour fills, though the left panel adds translucent glows and a ghosted chart. The thought-bubble contents are tiny and become a small blur at phone size. The white background keeps the frame open.
strength: A giant question headline with a stress-versus-confidence face pair frames the dilemma in two seconds.
weakness: The thought bubble holds the only DEBT illustration and is tiny, so the money-in-a-hat idea does not read at phone size.
bottleneck: The question sets investing against debt but never says which side wins, so the frame depends entirely on the viewer guessing the answer.
action: Hypothesis: label the two panels with a payoff and an investing return rate to test whether specific percentages sharpen the comparison.
counterexample: Seq 8 also splits two figures with different expressions but anchors them with numeric score cards, where this frame has no numbers.
expression_label: closed smile on left, sweating grimace on right
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: SECRETLY / GETTING RICH / 6 SIGNS / 1 SMALL START / 2 CONSISTENT GROWTH / 3 SMART SAVING / 4 FINANCIAL FREEDOM / 5 BUYING BACK TIME / 6 INVESTING IN HEALTH [icon sign: $1M]
scene: A cartoon man with grey-streaked dark hair, wide eyes and a big grin leans in from the left edge in a navy polo and khaki trousers, pointing across with his index finger. A row of six icons connected by green arrows runs along the bottom: a coin jar, a rising bar chart with an arrow, a pink piggy bank with a check mark, a green $1M sign, an alarm clock, and a heart with a pulse line and a plus badge. Each icon sits above a numbered circle and a two- or three-word label. A yellow tag reading 6 SIGNS sits above the row.
mechanism: A pre-answered checklist: the six numbered icons spell out the title's six signs as a left-to-right path from a small start to better health.
composition: The man occupies the left 25 percent at near full height, with a two-line headline over the upper centre and right. The 6 SIGNS tag sits in the middle and the icon strip runs the whole lower third, so the frame reads in three horizontal tiers. His pointing hand directs the eye along the strip.
typography: Three words in huge black capitals form the headline, a small black-on-yellow tag reads 6 SIGNS, and six short labels under the icons are in small grey-black capitals. The headline and the dollar sign survive at 160x90, but the numbered labels do not. The six labels hand over the signs the title only counts.
colors: An off-white background, black headline, navy shirt and a yellow tag, with green arrows and green accents tying the six icons together. The pink piggy bank and red heart are the only warm hues in the strip.
psychology: Wide eyes, a broad grin and a pointing hand give an inviting, upbeat instruction. The numbered sequence and the check mark add progress cues, and no alarm cue appears.
partnership: The title promises six signs you are secretly getting rich, and the thumbnail lists them in short form. It complements the title with the actual content, but the full list may satisfy the curiosity before the click.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: SECRETLY GETTING RICH first, then the grinning man and his pointing finger, then the yellow 6 SIGNS tag, and finally the icon strip left to right.
art: Smooth cartoon with consistent outlines and tidy icon illustrations, matching the character style of other thumbnails in the batch. The icon row is evenly spaced and coherent, and the character cutout is clean. The six labels and the numbers are tiny and blur out at phone size.
strength: The numbered icon path from a coin jar to a heart gives the six signs a clear left-to-right order.
weakness: Twenty-six words across the frame, with the six labels small, make the lower third read as noise at 160x90.
bottleneck: Spelling out all six signs removes the open question that the title sets up, leaving less reason to look further.
action: Hypothesis: keep only the first two icons and blank the rest with a question mark, to test whether withholding four signs lifts curiosity.
counterexample: Seq 9 shows the same character with only four words, where this frame stacks six labelled icons.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: YOUR SKIN REVEALS / DIABETES / 9 HIDDEN SIGNS
scene: A bald man with a grey beard and moustache, in blue scrubs with a stethoscope around his neck, looks at the viewer with slightly raised brows and parted lips while pointing his index finger toward the left. He stands in front of a solid red panel. At lower left, a rounded white-framed inset shows a close-up of a person's neck with darkened, thick, velvety skin outlined by a red glow and two small skin growths.
mechanism: A doctor-points-at-evidence frame: a scrubs-and-stethoscope figure and a skin close-up make the headline's claim that skin reveals diabetes feel observed.
composition: A black left panel carries the stacked text, a red right panel holds the large head-and-shoulders figure, and the inset image sits under the text at lower left. The figure's pointing finger aims across the seam toward the inset, so the viewer's gaze travels from face to hand to neck image. The three zones are cleanly separated.
typography: Seven words in three tiers: YOUR SKIN REVEALS in white, DIABETES in very large yellow capitals, and 9 HIDDEN SIGNS in white on a red bar. DIABETES is the dominant word and survives at 160x90, as do the other two lines. The text repeats the title's skin, diabetes and count and omits the age and doctor specialty.
colors: A black text panel, saturated red figure panel, yellow keyword and teal-blue scrubs. The red background and red bar act as an alarm colour, and the blue scrubs sit apart from the red field.
psychology: Slightly raised brows, parted lips, direct eye contact and a pointing finger read as a serious warning delivery. The red field and the close-up of altered skin add a health-threat cue.
partnership: The title offers nine skin signs of hidden diabetes from a cardiologist; the thumbnail states that skin reveals diabetes and shows one neck example. It complements the title with an image, but the printed claim is more definite than the title's wording, and the stethoscope does not name any specialty.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the yellow DIABETES word first, then the man's face on the red panel, then his pointing finger, and finally the neck inset at the lower left.
art: Photographic portrait with a very clean cutout against the flat red field, and a separate photo inset with a red glow overlaid on the neck skin. The mix of a studio portrait and a medical close-up is clearly composited, but the lighting on the face is consistent. Detail in the inset is lost at 160x90, but the shape and glow remain.
strength: A giant yellow DIABETES word plus a doctor pointing at a real-looking skin close-up make the medical topic and the stakes clear in a glance.
weakness: The nine signs are not shown, only one neck image, so the count is claimed but not illustrated.
bottleneck: The visual authority comes from scrubs and a stethoscope alone, with no name or specialty to back the cardiologist claim in the title.
action: Hypothesis: add a printed name and CARDIOLOGIST credential line on the scrubs, to test whether a visible credential matches the title's authority claim.
counterexample: Seq 6 shows the same diabetes angle with no person and a sole-and-ulcer image, where this frame puts a pointing practitioner in the centre.
expression_label: raised brows with parted lips and direct stare
hero_object: pointing man in scrubs with neck skin inset
medical_notes: The thumbnail says skin reveals diabetes and shows scrubs without a named credential, whereas the title attributes the warning to a cardiologist.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: SOMETIMES NICE TO SWIM IN (NOT NOW) / 4°C (NOT NICE TO SWIM IN)
scene: A tall portrait-format picture occupies the centre of the landscape frame, with dark brick-red bars on both sides. In it, a pink-red sky with faint wave lines holds a row of grey outlined clouds, with white forked lightning bolts hanging beneath them over a yellow band. Below a wavy horizontal line sit a dark red shark silhouette, a tiny fish and a small jellyfish-like shape, and the lower half is flat grey-olive with a 4°C label. Two small captions in a hand-lettered face sit over the picture.
mechanism: An unexplained diagram: a layered sky, storm and ocean with tongue-in-cheek swim captions raises a puzzle, but nothing in the frame states the Earth-stopping premise.
composition: A narrow vertical strip occupies roughly one third of the frame width and the rest is flat side bars. Within the strip the elements run in horizontal layers from sky to cloud band to waterline to a large empty grey base. The shark, fish and jellyfish are tiny and sit at the centre, while the lower half is empty.
typography: Fourteen words in two small captions of thin hand-lettered capitals, each only a few lines tall, placed at the centre of the strip. They are unreadable at 160x90, so no text survives. The captions describe swim conditions and say nothing about the title's spinning Earth.
colors: A warm pink-red sky blending into a yellow band and then a drab grey-olive base, flanked by dull brick-red side bars. Grey clouds and white lightning give the only contrast, and the dark red animal silhouettes are almost the same tone as the sky.
psychology: No person or face is shown. The lightning and storm clouds supply a mild hazard cue, but the scene is muted and the animals are too small to carry emotion.
partnership: The title asks what would happen if the Earth suddenly stopped spinning, and nothing in the frame names the Earth, spinning, or a consequence. The image can only be read as a swimming-conditions diagram, so it leaves the title's question unanswered and may need the title to make sense.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the grey cloud band with lightning first, then the small captions in the middle, then the tiny shark silhouette, and last the empty grey base.
art: A flat hand-drawn style with grainy texture and thin black outlines. The art is coherent, but the pillarbox bars and the small scale of the animal silhouettes waste most of the frame and leave little to see at small size.
strength: The bold colour bands of sky, storm and water give the strip a distinct, poster-like look among white-background thumbnails.
weakness: Both captions and all creatures are far too small to read at 160x90, and two thirds of the frame width is empty bars.
bottleneck: The picture shows no Earth, motion or subject that matches the title's question, so the thumbnail gives a viewer nothing to anchor the premise.
action: Hypothesis: crop to the cloud-and-shark layer and enlarge one caption to fill the full frame width, to test whether a legible subject beats the unused side bars.
counterexample: Seq 23 uses a bold white background with a big headline and a strong single illustration, where this frame has tiny captions inside a narrow strip.

scene: On a cream background, a large black glass pyramid at the left has a white light beam shooting straight up from its apex. In front of it sits a sphinx statue with a striped headdress on a gold entrance block, flanked by rows of palm trees. A fairytale castle with red, blue and white spires stands at the far left edge behind the palms. At the lower right, a strip of hotel towers and a street forms a skyline, and a thin red arrow links the two years under the headline.
mechanism: A landmark postcard with a time span: the pyramid, sphinx, castle and towers stand in for a city, and the 1905-to-2026 arrow frames a whole-history timeline.
composition: The pyramid takes the left half with its apex at the top-centre, and the headline block takes the right half at upper right. The skyline strip runs low across the right, so the layout reads as scenery on the left, text on the right and a horizontal city band underneath. The vertical light beam splits the cream sky.
typography: Four tokens in two tiers: LAS VEGAS in large black condensed capitals, with 1905 and 2026 joined by a thin red arrow beneath. The two years are also readable at 160x90. The title already gives the subject and a 13-minute length, and the thumbnail adds the start and end years.
colors: A warm cream field carries black text and a black pyramid with gold and sandy accents, a small blue-and-red castle and one red arrow. The low-saturation parchment look contrasts the black pyramid sharply.
psychology: No person is present, so the cues are place-based: the glowing beam and recognisable casino landmarks signal spectacle rather than any human emotion. The year span adds a sense of scope.
partnership: The title promises the entire history in 13 minutes, and the thumbnail turns the claim into a 1905-to-2026 arrow and a landmark scene. It complements the title with the year range, but the images show only modern buildings, so nothing from 1905 appears.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the black pyramid and its beam first, then LAS VEGAS at upper right, then the 1905-to-2026 line, and finally the skyline strip at lower right.
art: Clean flat illustration with bold outlines and a coherent cream-and-black palette, and the sphinx, palms and castle are consistent in style. Background detail on the right skyline is dense but small, while the large pyramid shape survives at 160x90.
strength: A black pyramid with a white beam is a single recognisable silhouette that places the topic without reading anything.
weakness: No 1905 imagery appears, so the arrow from 1905 to 2026 promises a change that the picture does not show.
bottleneck: The postcard-style landmark scene has no person or tension, so the frame announces a topic rather than a story.
action: Hypothesis: add a small desert-town scene under 1905 beside the skyline under 2026, to test whether a visible before-and-after pair makes the time span concrete.
counterexample: Seq 5 pairs a grey past against a colourful present in one frame, where this frame shows only the modern city beneath a year arrow.
hero_object: black pyramid with light beam and sphinx
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS
